title: EctD A163V: Temperature-controlled kinetic and titer study
abstractSummary: The study characterizes the EctD variant A163V, which catalyzes ectoine hydroxylation, evaluating its kinetic parameters and fermentation performance at 30°C.
researchQuestion: What are the kinetic and fermentation properties of the EctD variant A163V in the catalysis of ectoine hydroxylation?
mainFindings: Variant A163V exhibits a lower Michaelis constant (Km) for ectoine compared to the wild-type enzyme.
Fermentation using variant A163V at 30°C for 48 hours produced a product titer of 4.80 g/L.
The specific activity of variant A163V was 1.80 U/mg.
The product yield for variant A163V was 0.40 g/g substrate.
The volumetric productivity for variant A163V was 0.100 g/L/h.
methodsSummary: The researchers characterized the A163V variant of EctD at 30°C, measuring the Michaelis constant (Km) for ectoine and evaluating fermentation metrics including titer, specific activity, yield, and volumetric productivity.

limitations: The study did not test 35°C or 42°C cultivation.
Lower Km alone does not prove higher whole-process productivity.
No universal best variant is established.
shortSummary: Characterization of EctD variant A163V showing a reduced Km for ectoine (0.42 mM vs 0.80 mM for wild-type) and specific fermentation metrics including a titer of 4.80 g/L at 30°C.
